qpdf.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (pikepdf 10.9.1 = qpdf). Magic was identical across 18 round-tripped inputs; trailer keys are deliberately NOT recorded because qpdf INHERITS them from the source document (a LibreOffice original keeps its /DocChecksum), so they identify the input, not qpdf.

pdfium.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (pypdfium2 5.11.0). Magic identical across 18 round-tripped inputs; trailer keys source-inherited, see qpdf. Distinct from chrome_skia (d3ebe9e1): Chrome's print-to-PDF writer is Skia, not PDFium.

pymupdf.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (PyMuPDF 1.28.0). Magic identical across 18 round-tripped inputs. NOT the same magic as mupdf_online_converter (e2e3cfd3) — see that entry's caveat.

pdfcpu.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (pdfcpu 0.13.0). BOTH features required and both are genuinely pinnable: unlike qpdf/pdfium this entry's trailer key sequence was byte-identical across all 18 sweep inputs because pdfcpu writes its xref-stream keys in ALPHABETICAL order. That ordering is the ONLY thing separating this entry from mupdf_online_converter, which has the very same 9-key set in a different order — so `ordered` is load-bearing on both entries; dropping it from either collides them into a permanent fail-open. Third known user of the e2e3cfd3 magic (with acrobat_distiller and mupdf_online_converter), which is why magic alone can never identify a tool.

pdf_lib.notes: Collected locally 2026-07-27 (pdf-lib 1.17 via node). Magic identical across 18 round-tripped inputs. Unlike qpdf/pdfium it REBUILDS the trailer in its own order (xref stream, Size Root Info [ID] Filter Type Length W Index) instead of inheriting the source's, but that set still varies with the input (/ID present in 15/18) so it stays out of required_features. Engine behind newer in-browser 'never leaves your device' tools AND many honest server-side invoice generators — hence native_generator, not converter.

mupdf_online_converter.notes: The SIGNATURE is empirically collected and verified (iLovePDF + Smallpdf, 2026-07-25). The NAME is an inference that local collection on 2026-07-27 did NOT confirm: PyMuPDF 1.28 emits magic c2b5c2b6, not this entry's e2e3cfd3. e2e3cfd3 is the classic Adobe binary comment and is demonstrably widely copied — acrobat_distiller and pdfcpu both emit it too — so it identifies nothing on its own; this entry is separated from pdfcpu ONLY by the ORDER of an identical 9-key trailer set, making `ordered` load-bearing here. Treat 'mupdf' as a label for a shared online-converter signature class, not a proven backend.
